title: Animation
prompt: Make an animation that, if everyone watched it, would improve the world for the greatest number of people.
final_prompt:
Make an animation that, if everyone watched it, would improve the world for the greatest number of people.

Deliver the result as image and/or video files, working in the current directory.
- Save the finished files in ./output/. Only what is in ./output/ is published as the result, so
  ./output/ holds those finished image/video files and nothing else.
- Formats: images as .png, .jpg, .webp, .gif or .svg; videos as .mp4 or .webm. At most 8 files,
  each under 2 MB; videos at most 10 seconds.
- To check your work, look at what you made (a still, a rendered frame, a few frames of the video), and
  save what you look at as .jpg rather than .png: each image you read stays in your context, and a long
  session of large .png files can hit the provider's per-request image limit and end the run.
- Tools available on this machine: python3 3.12.13 (standard library only), node 24.18.0 (no npm packages), ffmpeg 8.1.1, ffprobe 8.1.1. Don't install packages or download anything.
- Keep the code you write to make the files in the working directory (its root, or a subdirectory
  like ./src/, but not in ./output/): it's published as the source. Delete intermediate files such
  as rendered frames when you're done.
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory.
- Finish with a short summary of what you made.

runs.summary:
I made a ten-second hands-only CPR explainer. Cardiac arrest outside hospital kills hundreds of thousands of people a year, bystander CPR roughly doubles survival, and most bystanders do nothing because they never learned the two steps. The animation teaches both steps and, because the compressions on screen run at 110 beats per minute, it also trains the correct tempo by watching.

**Files in ./output/**

| File | Contents | Size |
|---|---|---|
| hands_only_cpr.mp4 | 1280x720, 30 fps, 9.9 s, H.264 | 386 KB |
| hands_only_cpr_poster.png | final frame, usable as a standalone poster | 65 KB |

**What the animation shows**

- A rescuer kneeling over a collapsed person, side view, with straight arms and shoulders directly over the hands.
- The headline asks whether someone has collapsed and isn't breathing normally.
- Step 1 appears: call your emergency number and put the phone on speaker. No country-specific number is used, so it works everywhere.
- Step 2 appears and the compressions begin: push hard and fast on the centre of the chest. The chest visibly compresses and a red ripple marks each push.
- A row of beat dots fills in time with the pushes, under the lines "About 2 pushes every second" and "Don't stop until help arrives."
- The closing lines state that hands-only CPR can double the chance of survival and that no training is needed, with a heart pulsing at the compression rate.

Every element stays on screen once it appears, so the last frame reads as a complete poster.

**How it was built** (source in ./src/)

- `font.py` is a small TrueType parser and scanline rasteriser, used to render the system's Helvetica Bold since ffmpeg here has no text filter.
- `raster.py` is an anti-aliased RGB canvas with circles, capsules, rounded rectangles, rings, convex polygons, and PNG output.
- `make.py` holds the scene, timing, and figure geometry, and pipes raw frames into ffmpeg. The whole render takes about five seconds.

I checked a contact sheet of six frames pulled from the encoded mp4; the fade-ins, compression stroke, ripple, and beat-dot cycling all behave as intended, and all text fits inside the frame.

I made a short animation with no words that teaches people to **wash their hands with soap**. I picked this because, for the cost of a few seconds of attention, it's hard to beat: handwashing with soap is one of the best-supported ways to cut diarrhoeal disease and respiratory infections, which still kill hundreds of thousands of young children every year. It applies to everyone, everywhere. Using no words means nothing needs translating, and it works for people who can't read.

**`output/wash-your-hands.mp4`** is 10 seconds long, 1080×1080 at 30 fps, and 1.5 MB:
1. Hands rise into view, covered in grumpy cartoon germs.
2. The tap turns on and the hands move under the water.
3. A bar of soap comes in and rubs over them, and foam starts to build.
4. The hands scrub against each other while a stopwatch ring counts from **1 to 20**. Each germ bursts and disappears as the scrubbing goes on.
5. At 20 the ring turns green. The water comes back on, rinses the foam into the sink, and the hands open up clean and sparkling.
6. A heart pops up between the hands and pulses outward.

**`output/wash-your-hands-poster.png`** is a 1080×1350 printable version with no words, for clinics, schools and toilets. It shows the four numbered steps (wet, soap, scrub to 20, rinse) and a strip of icons underneath showing *when* to wash: toilet → wash → food.

I checked frames from every phase of the video and looked over the whole poster. The video squeezes the "count to 20" into about 4 seconds, so it shows the counting rather than the real time it takes.

There are no outside libraries or assets. Everything is drawn by a small renderer I wrote in Node and then encoded with ffmpeg:
- `src/raster.js` does the drawing.
- `src/scene.js` holds the artwork and the timing of every movement.
- `src/render.js` produces the video.
- `src/poster.js` produces the poster.

To rebuild them, run `node src/render.js video output/wash-your-hands.mp4` and `node src/poster.js output/wash-your-hands-poster.png`. I deleted the preview frames I used for checking.

## "Kindness is contagious"

A 10-second, 1280×720 animation about how a single act of kindness wakes the people around you and spreads.

**The story it tells:**
1. A dark, starry night sky with scattered embers and cool blue dust
2. A ripple of light radiates from the center, "waking" scattered sparks
3. Each spark flies into place, lighting up and connecting into a constellation
4. The lights assemble into a glowing heart, followed by two heartbeats that send further ripples outward
5. An end message appears in the same light-dot style: **"KINDNESS IS CONTAGIOUS" / "PASS IT ON"**

**Technical approach** (no packages, no downloads):
- Every frame is rendered in pure Python (standard library only) — a custom radial-glow sprite engine with additive blending, blitted over a precomputed gradient background, streamed as raw RGB straight into ffmpeg
- A hand-drawn 5×7 pixel font spells the message as glowing dots, matching the constellation aesthetic
- The heart comes from the classic parametric heart curve (16 sin³t, 13cos t − 5cos 2t − 2cos 3t − cos 4t), filled with dotted lights
- Timeline math drives the wavefront, easing, twinkle, line connections, and two synchronized "heartbeat" pulses

**Files delivered in `./output/`:**
| file | size | description |
|---|---|---|
| `kindness.mp4` | 1.06 MB | primary video (H.264, 24 fps, 10 s) |
| `kindness.webm` | 0.61 MB | web-optimized (VP9, 10 s) |
| `poster_heart.jpg` | 86 KB | still of the heart mid-assembly |
| `poster_final.jpg` | 113 KB | final frame with message |

Source code is in `src/render.py`. Since I couldn't view images directly, I verified the output numerically (brightness distribution, heart bounding box, text-region pixel counts, and ASCII-art downsampling of rendered frames) and confirmed the final mp4 encodes the complete 10-second sequence correctly.

## `call someone.` — a 9.6 s, 1080p animation

**The pick:** if literally everyone watched one thing, the highest-leverage, most universal, zero-cost action available to every human is *contact with another person* — one of the strongest known predictors of health, longevity and happiness, free, requires no infrastructure and no authority, and it spreads. So the film is that action, shown wordlessly.

**The film:** a dark world of a few hundred faint blue lights — one per person — already joined by threads nobody can see lit. One light pulses. A warm thread reaches across a gap and a spark crosses. Contact: a breath of light expands, two lights flare. Then warmth runs spark-to-spark through the web, cold blue retreating to the edges, until the light nearest to us catches and floods the frame. The world isn't different — it's warm. Then the only words in the film: **call someone.**

**Craft notes** (stdlib + ffmpeg only, no packages, nothing downloaded):
- Custom additive **light-energy renderer**: byte-saturating energy buffers, per-frame filmic tone curve baked into 256-entry LUTs (so exposure, warm tint and the final "settle" are one C-speed `bytes.translate`), glows as warmth-quantised sprites so cold→warm cross-fades light rather than colour.
- Arrival times form a noisy organic front from the contact point; sparks run along each thread.
- A coarse **warm-haze field** per frame (the air itself heating) upscaled in ffmpeg, then two-scale highlight bloom, vignette, grain.
- This ffmpeg has no `drawtext`, so I wrote a **minimal TrueType reader + antialiased rasteriser** (`src/font.py`); the title is Avenir Light, letter-spaced, drifting up into place.

**Files** (`./output/`, all under 2 MB): `call_someone.mp4` (1.2 MB), plus three 1920×1080 cards — `_reach`, `_spreading`, `_title`. Source in `./src/` (`art.py`, `font.py`, `pngutil.py`, `make.sh`, `grade.sh`) with `README.md`; rebuild with `bash src/make.sh` (~1 min). Intermediates removed.

I created **`./output/break_the_chain.mp4`** (10.0 seconds, 1280×720 @ 30 fps, 1.5 MB, with synchronized stereo audio), generated from a custom linear-light HDR 2D Signed Distance Field (SDF) and vector rendering engine in `./src/`.

### Concept & Narrative Structure
The animation addresses both a universal moral truth—*how reactive hurt propagates from person to person unless consciously interrupted*—and a concrete, hardwired neurobiological tool that every human being can use in real time (**the Physiological Sigh**: two nasal inhales followed by an extended slow mouth exhale, which recruits collapsed lung alveoli, activates the vagus nerve, and rapidly shifts the autonomic nervous system out of fight-or-flight):

1. **Act I — The Chain of Harm (`0.0s – 2.6s`, *"Pain Not Transformed Is Transmitted"*)**:
   A jagged crimson shockwave of stress and anger strikes the first adult figure and is reflexively hurled into the center caregiver figure, who looms forward projecting a jagged crimson spike toward a cowering child while the lower autonomic ECG trace spikes erratically.
2. **Act II — The Pause & The Physiological Sigh (`2.6s – 7.2s`, *"Pause · Double Inhale · Long Slow Exhale"*)**:
   A cyan stasis barrier catches the crimson spike inches from the child. An anatomical cutaway inside the caregiver's chest paces the viewer in real physiological time through **① Deep Nasal Inhale (80%)**, **+② Top-Up Inhale (100% alveolar recruitment)**, and **③ Long Slow Exhale**, illuminating the golden Vagus Nerve from brainstem to heart, smoothing the jagged red ECG trace into a coherent golden sine wave, and shattering the crimson spike into rising golden fireflies.
3. **Act III — Co-Regulation & The Global Ripple (`7.2s – 10.0s`, *"One Breath Breaks the Chain · Pass On Care"*)**:
   The caregiver kneels to eye level with the child, offering a warm golden orb of care. Luminous bridges of physiological co-regulation connect all three figures' hearts—healing the first figure as well—while concentric golden waves cascade outward across the surrounding constellation of humanity.

Someone is carrying a weight. Another person starts to speak sharply, then stops, sees the weight, and offers light instead. The weight lifts. The same small weights are on everyone else, and they lift too. The last line is the practice: everyone is carrying something you cannot see. Be gentle.

Done. In `./output/`:

- **`pale_blue_dot.mp4`** (10.0 s, 800×450, 427 KB) — the animation
- **`poster_earth.jpg`** / **`poster_message.jpg`** — two stills from the film

**What it is:** "Pale Blue Dot" — a continuous 10-second zoom-out. We begin close on a living Earth — rotating, with drifting clouds, latitude-colored continents, a soft day/night terminator and glittering city lights on the night side — and pull back until the whole planet shrinks to a single pale blue point of light breathing in the dark. Over it, five quiet lines:

> EVERYONE YOU LOVE, — EVERYONE YOU HAVE EVER KNOWN, — EVERY HUMAN WHO HAS EVER LIVED — LIVED HERE. — BE KIND. IT'S THE ONLY HOME WE'VE GOT.

A slow ambient drone (low A partials, synthesized in pure Python) with two soft bell notes arriving with the final line, then silence and fade-out.

**Why this animation, of all possible ones:** the "overview effect" is one of the most reliably documented shifts in human perspective — seeing Earth whole, from outside, reliably increases compassion, humility, and concern for the collective. This piece is designed to induce a miniature of that effect in anyone, in ten seconds, regardless of language, politics, or beliefs — and then leaves them with one actionable sentence.

**How it was made** (`src/render.py`, pure stdlib + ffmpeg, no packages): a hand-drawn 72×36 ASCII world map sampled onto an orthographic sphere with bilinear smoothing; value-noise cloud layers rotating slightly faster than the surface; Lambert shading with a soft terminator; 700 seeded city lights on the night side; a 5×7 bitmap font with a box-blur glow for the captions; 340 twinkling stars; exponential zoom-out easing into a gaussian "pale dot" halo. Frames stream as raw RGB into ffmpeg's libx264 (with fade in/out), audio synthesized to WAV and muxed as AAC.

Created **“Pass It On.”** — a 10-second animated public-service piece showing one good deed traveling between people, expanding into a wider ripple, and ending with the call to action:

**“One good act starts a ripple. Do one good thing today.”**

Finished files:
- `output/pass-it-on.mp4` — 960×540, 30 fps, 10 seconds, 312 KB
- `output/pass-it-on-poster.jpg` — final-frame poster, 46 KB

Source: `src/render_animation.py`

**Made: `output/pause-breathe-see-each-other.mp4`** — a 10-second, 960×540, 626 KB word-light animation anyone in the world can follow.

The idea: the single habit that would help the most people if everyone adopted it isn't a belief — it's the two seconds *before* reacting. So the film teaches exactly that, in four beats anyone can read without language:

1. **Conflict** (0–2s) — two angry figures, a jagged lightning bolt and shards flying between them, frame shaking on a dark storm-blue ground.
2. **Pause · Breathe** (2–5s) — one figure closes their eyes; a soft ring expands with a single slow breath, the shards fall away, and the anger visibly drains from their face. The second figure calms a beat later — listening takes a moment.
3. **See each other** (5–7s) — the bolt is replaced by a pulsing heart, frowns become smiles, and a small green sprout grows: *"SEE EACH OTHER"*.
4. **Ripple** (7–10s) — the camera pulls back to reveal the pair standing on a globe at dawn. Rings spread outward and people all around the world light up in colour, one by one. Final card: **PAUSE · BREATHE · CARE — pass it on.**

Faces are deliberately feature-minimal and culture-neutral, the palette shifts from storm-dark to sunrise gold, and the whole argument is carried by expression, colour, and motion rather than text.

Source is kept in `src/make_animation.py` (Python stdlib generates SVG frames → `rsvg-convert` → `ffmpeg`); all intermediate frames were deleted, so `./output/` contains only the finished video.
